root_cause: The dispatch block handles only one customer per tick, so after an inline zero-duration Finish the loop either advances to a later arrival or breaks on (None, None), leaving queued customers unprocessed.
general_lesson: Drain all immediately executable work before advancing time, and ensure termination checks account for pending queues.

root_cause: The dispatch block handles only one customer per iteration, so after an inline zero-duration Finish the next iteration ignores the remaining queue and breaks when no arrival or scheduled completion remains.
general_lesson: After instantaneous completion, continue processing ready work before advancing time or terminating; include pending work in termination decisions.

root_cause: parse_number receives an item slice and returns item-relative LeadingZero and NumberOverflow offsets without adding item_start, so both failing tests report offset 2 instead of field-relative offset 4.
general_lesson: Track coordinate origins when parsing slices, and translate helper error offsets into the required coordinate system before propagating them.

root_cause: parse_number reports item-relative offsets without adding item_start, causing both numeric-error offset failures, while parse_field leaves end_value equal to start_value for stepped single numbers, causing both selection failures.
general_lesson: Track slice origins when reporting offsets, and verify each syntax variant’s selection boundaries against every explicit requirement.

root_cause: parse_field validates steps before base endpoints and range ordering, causing both precedence failures, reports the empty step in */ at offset 2 instead of item start 0, and next_fire scans every minute while recomputing weekdays from 2000, causing the impossible-schedule timeout.
general_lesson: Validate complete syntax before numbers, enforce specified error precedence and locations, and assess worst-case search complexity for inputs with no solution.

root_cause: parse_field validates the step before numeric endpoints and range ordering, masking required base errors, while next_fire scans every remaining minute and recomputes weekdays, timing out on impossible schedules.
general_lesson: Implement explicit validation precedence and assess worst-case search cost, especially when proving that no result exists.

root_cause: parse_item validates step values before base bounds and range ordering, masking required numeric and named-range errors, while next_fire scans every minute and matches recomputes weekdays from 2000 each time, causing sparse and impossible schedules to time out.
general_lesson: Separate syntax checks from ordered semantic validation, and assess worst-case search complexity across the full supported domain.

root_cause: parse_field passes endpoint positions to endpoint(), causing 99-JUNK/0 to report InvalidSyntax at offset 3 instead of item offset 0, and uses numeric_end.unwrap_or(item_offset) for reversed named ranges, incorrectly reporting the item start instead of the end atom start.
general_lesson: Track item starts and operand starts separately, and verify each error variant uses the location explicitly required by its contract.

root_cause: integer_syntax accepts -0 because its zero branch checks only that the digit ends the string, so both failing tests omit the required InvalidInteger errors.
general_lesson: Validate explicitly forbidden spellings before numeric conversion, and check signed zero separately from unsigned zero.

root_cause: extract_columns breaks the spec loop immediately after a Stop error and pushes the partially built row without filling remaining spec positions with None.
general_lesson: When stopping evaluation early, preserve the required output shape by initializing or padding all unevaluated positions.

root_cause: parse_decimal parses the unsigned magnitude into i64 before negating, rejecting the valid i64::MIN endpoint, while extract_columns breaks immediately on a Stop error without filling the remaining requested positions with None.
general_lesson: Check both signed numeric endpoints and preserve required output dimensions when evaluation stops early.

root_cause: For interior empty labels, candidate.rs reports pos_at(clean, start.saturating_sub(1), input.len()), selecting the preceding dot instead of the second dot at start.
general_lesson: Check error offsets against each explicitly specified boundary case, especially adjacent delimiters, rather than reusing the preceding delimiter’s position.

root_cause: validate_path uses i.saturating_sub(1) for every empty component, reporting interior repeated slashes one byte early, although that subtraction is correct for trailing empty components.
general_lesson: Handle interior and trailing empty components separately, and verify reported offsets against explicit examples before coding.

root_cause: roman_decode selects uppercase whenever any uppercase byte exists, so "xivI" reports MixedCase at index 0 instead of using the first byte's lowercase case and reporting index 3.
general_lesson: When validation depends on the first element, derive the reference condition from that element rather than searching the entire input.

root_cause: Both parse magnitude loops use unchecked u128 multiplication and addition before checking bounds, so sufficiently long numerator or denominator tokens panic instead of returning OutOfRange at the required offset.
general_lesson: When parsing unbounded digit sequences into fixed-width integers, detect overflow during accumulation rather than checking bounds only afterward.

root_cause: parse_magnitude uses unchecked u128 multiplication and addition, panicking on long numerator or denominator tokens, while transpose and Matrix::mul iterate enormous outer dimensions even when their inner dimensions are zero, causing timeouts.
general_lesson: Bound numeric accumulation before overflow, and short-circuit empty operations before entering loops whose bounds can be arbitrarily large.

root_cause: parse_magnitude accumulates arbitrarily long digit sequences with unchecked u128 multiplication before checking bounds, causing both parsing panics, while transpose and Matrix::mul iterate enormous outer dimensions despite empty inner dimensions, causing both timeouts.
general_lesson: Handle unbounded numeric input without overflowing, and ensure empty computations terminate independently of unused dimension sizes.

root_cause: transpose iterates self.cols even when self.rows is zero, and mul iterates self.rows even when rhs.cols is zero, causing both failing tests to traverse usize::MAX empty inner loops.
general_lesson: Handle empty results before dimension-driven loops so runtime depends on actual entries rather than unused dimensions.

root_cause: parse_magnitude accumulates arbitrarily long tokens with unchecked u128 multiplication before checking bounds, causing both parse panics, while transpose and Matrix::mul iterate huge outer dimensions despite empty inner dimensions, causing both timeouts.
general_lesson: Check numeric limits during accumulation, and short-circuit empty work before entering loops over potentially enormous dimensions.

root_cause: transpose and mul iterate huge outer dimensions despite empty outputs, while solve allocates is_pivot and collects free columns before checking particular and basis shape overflow, causing timeouts and a capacity-overflow panic.
general_lesson: Handle empty shapes without dimension-sized loops, and validate all required output sizes before allocating auxiliary structures.

root_cause: transpose and mul iterate enormous outer dimensions despite empty inner dimensions, causing timeouts, while solve allocates free-column storage before checking n*(n-rank) for basis-shape overflow, causing a capacity-overflow panic instead of ShapeOverflow.
general_lesson: Short-circuit empty work after required validation, and check every derived output size before allocating auxiliary storage.

root_cause: shortest_lex_route evaluates distance[candidate] + 1 for unreachable neighbors whose distance remains usize::MAX, causing overflow and panicking during valid route queries.
general_lesson: Guard unreachable-distance sentinels before arithmetic, and check route selection when outgoing branches cannot reach the destination.

root_cause: build_lines omits separator_cost from hyphen opportunity fitting and unused-column calculations, so hidden_one_below_tie computes 2² + 14 instead of 1² + 14 and incorrectly flushes the line.
general_lesson: Include all emitted separators when calculating candidate fit and remaining space, while preserving explicitly different baseline formulas.

root_cause: Both optimizers generate marker splits only for the starting word, and optimize additionally requires that word to exceed capacity, excluding the complete-word-plus-marker-prefix layouts needed by all five failing tests.
general_lesson: Enumerate every permitted transition before optimizing, including optional splits after earlier complete items and splits of items that already fit.

root_cause: The ordinary-host branch calls parse_port with ? before validating host_text, so s://ab!c:xx returns InvalidPort at 9 instead of InvalidHost at 6.
general_lesson: Separate structural splitting from validation, and validate fields in the specified order when multiple fields can be invalid.

root_cause: The ordinary-host branch calls parse_port with ? before validating host_text, so s://ab!c:xx returns InvalidPort at 9 instead of InvalidHost at 6.
general_lesson: Separate structural splitting from validation, and validate fields in the specified order before propagating errors.

root_cause: parse_authority calls parse_port before validating the ordinary host, causing port errors to mask invalid hosts, while resolve_url's empty-reference early return retains the base fragment instead of clearing it.
general_lesson: Validate fields in the specified order, and check early returns against every inheritance and default rule.

root_cause: candidate.rs validates ordinary ports before hosts, passes the IPv6 port colon's offset instead of the following byte's offset to parse_port, and splits the fully decoded path on '/', causing encoded slashes to misalign raw segments and navigation operations.
general_lesson: Verify validation order and offset origins explicitly, and split raw structure before decoding individual segments so escaped delimiters remain data.

root_cause: decode_many calls Vec::with_capacity(count) before decoding, so count = usize::MAX panics with capacity overflow instead of returning the first integer's Truncated error on empty input.
general_lesson: Do not preallocate directly from unbounded requested counts; grow storage as valid results arrive so impossible capacities cannot preempt required errors.

root_cause: decode_many calls Vec::with_capacity(count) before decoding, so count = usize::MAX causes a capacity-overflow panic instead of returning the first integer's Truncated error on empty input.
general_lesson: Avoid allocating directly from untrusted counts before validating available input; distinguish capacity arithmetic overflow from allocation exhaustion.

root_cause: decode_many calls Vec::with_capacity(count) before decoding, so count == usize::MAX causes a capacity-overflow panic instead of returning Truncated for empty input.
general_lesson: Avoid preallocating directly from unchecked request sizes; validate available input or grow output incrementally so extreme sizes preserve required error behavior.

root_cause: decode_many calls Vec::with_capacity(count) before decoding, so count == usize::MAX panics with capacity overflow instead of returning the first integer's Truncated error for empty input.
general_lesson: Avoid allocating directly from unchecked request counts; process available input first so extreme counts return required errors without capacity panics.
